title: Chicken Tikka (Batch)
subtitle: Indian batch. 4 servings. 10 min prep + 30 min marinate, 20 min cook.

ingredients.thai_market_tip: Tops 1kg tray. Thigh stays juicy through the marinade-and-air-fry. Breast dries out.
FAGE or Gaia tub at Tops. Strained, not the runny 'Greek-style' local brand.
Patak's tikka masala paste at Tops Indian/world food aisle. Save loose-spice mixing for the weekend.
Eastern brand sachet. Extra layer on top of the paste.

ingredients.note: For colour without heat — skip if not available.
For greasing the air fryer basket.

substitutions.note: Higher protein, leaner. Marinate full 60 min minimum or it'll go chalky.
Press 30 min, cube, marinate. Drops protein to ~33g/svg — pair with dal to hit target.

steps.text: Whisk yogurt, tikka paste, lemon juice, garlic, ginger, garam masala, Kashmiri chili in a large bowl.
Add chicken chunks. Toss until every piece is fully coated. Cover, fridge 30 min minimum, 4 hours ideal.
Preheat air fryer 200°C / 400°F, 3 min. Brush basket lightly with 1 tsp oil.
Shake excess marinade off chicken. Lay in single layer in air fryer — work in 2 batches if needed.
Air fry 9 min, shake basket, another 6–8 min until edges are charred and internal 75°C / 165°F.
Rest 3 min. Portion into 4 containers. Cilantro and lemon wedge per portion. Keeps 4 days fridge, 2 months freezer.

serves_with.note: Greek yogurt + cucumber + cumin. Free macros.

notes: Patak's tikka paste is genuinely good — there's no shame in skipping the home-blended spice mix. Greek yogurt does two jobs: it tenderises through proteolysis (the lactic acid breaks down chicken proteins) AND adds 8g protein per serving. Don't skip the marinate time; 30 min is the floor.
